slides.bubble: Why does ChatGPT forget what I said 10 minutes ago in our chat?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: The Context Window 🧠
slides.bubble: LLMs have no ongoing memory. Each reply re-reads earlier text in a context window.

slides.speaker: byte
slides.title: What Happens When Full? 🛑
slides.bubble: What happens when that context window reaches its token limit?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Silent Eviction ✂️
slides.bubble: Older messages are dropped off from the start, so the model literally cannot see them!

slides.speaker: byte
slides.title: How To Fix It? 💡
slides.bubble: So prompt summaries or vector databases keep long chats alive?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Keep Prompts Lean ⚡
slides.bubble: Exactly! Prune system prompts and summarize key points before the window overflows.

takeaway: ChatGPT doesn't have human memory. When the context window fills up, older messages silently disappear.
caption:
🧠 DID YOU KNOW? 🤯

Ever wonder why ChatGPT forgets what you said 20 minutes ago?

Here is how LLM memory actually works:
🔹 LLMs store zero memory between turns.
🔹 Every response re-reads your previous messages in a 'context window'.
🔹 Once that window fills, older tokens are silently discarded!
